questions.history: Send one request through the original and one through the clone
questions.prediction: Both originals should deliver [A]. The parent clone should deliver no X-Step value, while the merged clone should deliver [A], each reaching the terminal handler exactly once.
questions.basis: Cloning a configured builder is expected to retain the original handler behavior. The downstream header observation demonstrates that the decorator ran.
questions.refutation: The merged clone loses or duplicates A or completion occurs without the terminal handler observing its request.

questions.history: Build an undecorated builder and its untouched clone and call both
questions.prediction: On both revisions neither handler adds X-Step and each reaches the terminal handler once.
questions.basis: In the absence of a decorator the same public chain handles both requests.
questions.refutation: Either handler acquires a spurious marker or drops a request.

questions.history: After cloning the A-configured builder, register B only on the clone and C only on the original. Send a fresh request through each
questions.prediction: On the merge the clone should deliver [A,B] and the original [A,C], in that order, each once. Another independent clone of the original should observe [A,C].
questions.basis: Composition applies the previously registered outer decorator first. Extending one builder replaces its composed function without changing its sibling.
questions.refutation: Either builder loses A, inherits its sibling’s private marker, reverses the markers or invokes the terminal handler twice.
